historical_references.reference: Al-Shafi'i was a major figure in the development of Sunni Islamic law in the 9th century. He was born in Gaza and studied under the great jurist Malik ibn Anas in Medina. He later returned to Iraq and founded the Shafi'i school of thought, which became one of the four major Sunni schools of Islamic law.

Al-Shafi'i is known for his work in compiling and organizing the Hadith, or sayings and actions of the Prophet Muhammad. His collection, Al-Umm, was one of the first major works to systematically categorize Hadith according to legal topics, and it became a foundational text for the Shafi'i school of thought.
